title: Building Foundation Models via Weight-Space Programming (WSP): Analytical Alignment, Multi-Donor Cognitive Grafting, and Closed-Form Refusal Abliteration without Backpropagation
read_level: full (5-page PDF and the longer Markdown version in the same record); figures not inspected
metadata_mismatch: Concept DOI 23958069 resolves to version record 23958070 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23958070). Metadata title 'Building foundational models using Weight Space Programming' differs from paper title. Metadata creator 'Quillan-Ronin Research Team' vs paper 'Quillan-Ronin Sovereign Research Laboratory' (PDF and MD); PDF footer also says 'Quillan-Ronin Sovereign Laboratory'. Paper gives only 'November 2026'; date taken from Zenodo publication_date. Record description is written in first person singular ('how i used Weight Space Programming').
why_wsp: Self-labelled 'Weight-Space Programming' framework of closed-form, gradient-free weight operations (refusal-direction projection, SVD grafting of donor weights, MoE folding) applied by the authors without an LLM editor; counts as a non-LLM alternative explicitly positioned as WSP.
domain: LLM refusal removal, multi-donor weight merging, inference compilation (Llama 3.2 1B base)
editor: none (closed-form linear algebra: contrastive-mean refusal direction, orthogonal projection, truncated SVD, ternary quantization)
target: Llama 3.2 1B Instruct base with grafted adapters from Falcon 3 1B, BitNet 1.58b Large, Qwen 2.5/3.5; output described as 'Sovereign 1.2B' model
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Refusal projection applied to W_down "across layers 12 through 15"; no count given

headline_results.claim: Throughput of quantized GGUF output vs PyTorch FP16
headline_results.quote: WSP closed-form GGUF compilation accelerates generation from 3.94 to 48.00 tok/s (12.18x) while dropping peak VRAM from 2,842 MB to 1,024 MB.
WSP synthesizes a calibrated Sovereign 1.2B foundation model in under 180 seconds
To verify the elimination of corporate refusal behaviors, models were tested against contrastive queries known to trigger false-positive safety refusals
headline_results.where: MD Sec. 7.2 (three example prompts, no counts)

cost.quote: This analytical projection executes in O(d · dffn) operations (≈16.7 MFLOPs per layer), requiring under 2 milliseconds on CPU.

baselines_and_controls: Throughput only: PyTorch FP16 baseline and fused static KV-cache FP16 vs Q4_K_M GGUF; refusal comparison vs base Llama 3.2 1B Instruct on three prompts. No accuracy benchmarks reported despite abstract claim of 'zero degradation in benchmark logic' (MD).
runs_and_variance: single run / not reported (64-token generation on one prompt for throughput)
robustness_of_edits: not tested (GGUF quantization is part of the pipeline but its effect on behavior is not measured)
verification: Theorem 1 (linearity of MoE folding) with a one-line proof; no empirical verification of claimed parity
limitations_stated: Folding assumes additive low-rank updates (SVD truncation error rises for r > d/2); non-linear residual connections cannot be collapsed across layers.
notes_for_survey: Uses the WSP name for refusal abliteration plus weight merging; does not cite Takehi et al. and has no LLM editor. Evidence is a throughput table and three qualitative refusal examples. No statement on AI authorship in the record or paper.
